title: ephemeral-route-signatures-and-stream-keepalive-auth
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Multiple customers reported production instability for long-lived streaming tool calls routed through intermediate proxies and gateway layers. When combined with scoped project keys and browser CORS preflight behavior, signed stream handshakes were either blocked or expired mid-stream, causing expensive reconnections. This PR introduces an ephemeral per-route signature token, a lightweight stream keepalive header, and an OpenAI-compat mapping so existing integrations keep working.

What this changes: 1) Introduces the X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token header (opaque, short TTL ~30s) that is minted by the control plane during initial handshake for streaming/tool-call sessions. The token is bound to a specific route+method and is micro-rotated on reconnects. 2) Adds X-RDW-Stream-Pulse: a keepalive pingable header that clients can emit periodically to prevent proxy idle timeouts without extending the main auth TTL. 3) Implements per-route signed-allowlist metadata stored in route config (allowlisted tool endpoints that accept ephemeral tokens) and a fallback mapping layer for OpenAI-compatible Authorization: Bearer semantics (ephemeral token presented as Bearer for compat if requested). 4) Refines CORS preflight behavior: control plane replies to OPTIONS with X-RDW-Allow-Ephemeral and exposes X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token in Access-Control-Expose-Headers when a handshake is expected from browser contexts. 5) Adds server-side validation hooks that check nonce replays and small KV entry to track ephemeral token rotations for up to 60s to support short reconnect windows.

Compatibility notes: - Default behavior is backward compatible: existing long-lived API keys/Project tokens continue to work; ephemeral tokens are optional and preferred for streaming/browser tool-calls. - OpenAI-compat: when clients use Authorization: Bearer <token> for streaming endpoints, the gateway will accept ephemeral tokens presented as Bearer and transparently mark the session as ephemeral for routing decisions. - For Dedicated/Private deployments, ephemeral token minting is disabled by default but can be toggled via config:enable_ephemeral_handshake.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for token minting, rotation, and expiry (90% coverage for handshake modules). - Integration tests covering browser OPTIONS preflight -> ephemeral token exchange -> streaming reconnect. - Load test (benchmark-lab) shows <3% added p99 latency on handshake paths and no measurable change on steady-state token-bearing streams. - Added new e2e scenario to perf-canary to simulate proxy-induced mid-stream reconnects; regression prevented in 95% of runs.

Security considerations: ephemeral tokens are short-lived and single-route-scoped; the server enforces strict nonce reuse checks so tokens cannot be replayed across routes. We log handshake failures and surface an alert when token mint rate exceeds expected traffic patterns (possible replay or abuse).

Deployment plan: staged rollout on Canary -> blue/green in Hosted -> opt-in for Dedicated/Private with feature flag. Config defaults off for Private. Gate: metrics for handshake success rate and p95 handshake latency must be within SLOs before wide rollout.

release_notes: Introduce ephemeral per-route handshake tokens (X-RDW-Ephemeral-Token) for more resilient browser and proxy streaming.
Add X-RDW-Stream-Pulse keepalive header to reduce proxy-induced reconnects.
OpenAI-compat: accept ephemeral tokens presented as Bearer headers for streaming endpoints.
New console flag: enable_ephemeral_handshake (off by default for Private).
comments: Aisha Patel: Overall this looks good. A couple of questions: how do we surface ephemeral token mint failures to customers? Can we add a counter metric?
Maya Chen: Added rdw.handshake.mint_fail counter in the latest commit and an alert rule draft in docs/handshake/alerts.md. Also included a console UI note in docs so SREs can toggle the flag.
Marco Li: Why not use long-lived signed cookies for browser flows to avoid repeated OPTIONS calls?

Maya Chen: We considered cookies but they don't map cleanly to our gateway routing model and introduce CSRF surface; ephemeral token in header allows consistent routing and simple CORS expose. Added a short section to the design doc explaining the tradeoffs.
Sofia Ramos (approval): Verified integration tests and perf-canary output; approving pending small nits about log text (addressed).
notes: Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2123/ephemeral-handshake-design - see section 'Browser handshake flow' for diagrams. Perf reports attached in CI artifacts.
